# Mixture-of-widths

Per-depth deflation of each block's inner rank over the recurrent loop (a helically-precessing low-rank slice), turning deep recurrence into a population of narrow voters. The ``helical`` variants mask channels under a full matmul, which proves the dynamics; the ``helical_sparse`` variants slice the weights so the matmul shrinks, a real FLOP reduction.

Namespace: ``registry.namespace("width")``, declared in ``praxis.width`` (7 entries)

Selected with ``--width-type`` (default: unset).

## `helical`, `helical_late`, `helical_steady`, `helical_tight` - HelicalWidth

Deflate each dense block to a helically-precessing low-rank slice per recurrent step, on
a raised-sine arch over depth (inflate early, decay the tail). ``floor`` is the minimum
width fraction; ``peak`` is the depth fraction where width crests. An ``nn.Module`` (no
parameters of its own) so it appears on the architecture blueprint.

Source: [praxis/width/helical.py:80](../praxis/width/helical.py#L80)

Presets:
- `helical` - Mask variant on the default arch: inflates early (peak 0.3) with a width floor of 0.25.
- `helical_late` (`peak=0.6`) - ``helical`` with the width crest moved mid-stack (peak 0.6).
- `helical_steady` (`floor=0.5, peak=0.5`) - ``helical`` with floor and peak both 0.5: a gentle breathing that never drops below half width.
- `helical_tight` (`floor=0.1, peak=0.25`) - ``helical`` with aggressive deflation: floor 0.1, crest at 0.25 of depth.

## `helical_sparse`, `helical_sparse_tight` - HelicalSparseWidth

Truly-sparse helical deflation: same arch schedule as ``HelicalWidth``, but it slices
the GLU and attention-head weights so the matmuls actually shrink instead of masking
them.

Source: [praxis/width/sparse.py:139](../praxis/width/sparse.py#L139)

Presets:
- `helical_sparse` - Sparse variant on ``helical``'s default arch: sliced weights and a smaller matmul, so the FLOP saving is real.
- `helical_sparse_tight` (`floor=0.1, peak=0.25`) - ``helical_tight``'s schedule (floor 0.1, peak 0.25) on the sparse, sliced-weight implementation.

## `none` - FullWidth

No-op width policy. The full model runs at full rank every step - the default, selected
by ``--width-type none``. An ``nn.Module`` (carrying no parameters) so it shows on the
architecture blueprint like any other piece.

Source: [praxis/width/base.py:8](../praxis/width/base.py#L8)
